saints.name: St. Isidore of Seville
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The last of the Latin Fathers, whose learning gathered the wisdom of the ancient world for a new age…
biography: Born at Cartagena about 560, Isidore belonged to a family of saints: his brothers Leander and Fulgentius and his sister Florentina are all venerated. Educated in the cathedral school of Seville, he succeeded Leander as archbishop in 600 and governed that see for more than thirty years.

He laboured to weld Goths and Romans into one Catholic people, completing the conversion of the Visigoths from Arianism. He presided over the Second Council of Seville in 619 and over the Fourth Council of Toledo in 633, which ordered every bishop to establish a school in his cathedral city for the study of the liberal arts.

His Etymologies, an encyclopedia in twenty books, preserved the learning of antiquity and was the most popular compendium in medieval libraries; he also wrote a history of the Goths. He died on 4 April 636 and was proclaimed Doctor of the Church in 1722. Because he gathered all knowledge for learners, he is patron of students and has even been proposed as patron of the Internet.
saints.knownFor: His Etymologies and his labour to preserve ancient learning.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctor of the Church (1722)

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 4 April
